identity.description:
D16 documents: Codex in CI, and the staff reviewer design

D16 as documents, for the user to read before any code. Docs only: no code change, no version change.

## Documents

- `docs/research/d16-codex-in-ci.md` (part b): can the Codex CLI run in CI on a ChatGPT subscription? The vendor documents it but says "The right way to authenticate automation is with an API key" and "Do not use this workflow for public or open-source repositories", and "Do not share the same file across concurrent jobs or multiple machines". The note gives four options with what the tool and the user must do: (A) a self-hosted private runner, (B) a GitHub-hosted job with the login file in a secret (fragile: the file refreshes after about 8 days), (C) an API key, about $0.11 to $0.20 a review at the list price of Sol 6.2, (D) the reviewer runs only on a machine with a logged-in Codex CLI. pr-review itself is public, so it cannot use A or B.
- `docs/design/staff-reviewer.md` (parts a and c): a reviewer of `kind: codex` in a prompt file; selected like the others, opt-in by config; it never fails a review (skip or failure with a reason in the summary); a 10-minute guard limit that kills the process group; first and fresh runs only; a sandbox of a tree with no `.git`, a small environment, read-only, no network setting, and `redact` on its output; the record fields. Refactor recommendations leave the findings list before the verifier, take a truth check with a new prompt, at most two, one PR comment edited on each first or fresh run, an off switch, a record stage, and hand-free eval counts.

Each document states the open questions for the user at the top. The most important one: the read-only sandbox of Codex stops writes but not reads, so a steered review could put a secret into a finding. The design lowers that risk and cannot remove it.

One critic round on the design: its 12 findings are applied (the read scope of the sandbox, later runs, a new truth-check prompt, the loader and schema changes, the config default of `enabled`, the record fields, the process-group kill, the strict tag parse, the limit before the truth check, the comment mechanics, the eval checks).
